title: A railroad official's daughter
text: Rosamond got its name from a Southern Pacific Railroad official who named the town after his daughter. The rails reached Rosamond in 1876, as they did in Tehachapi and Mojave. Rosamond was established in 1877 as a townsite owned by the Southern Pacific Railroad. During the 1890s, gold was discovered in the area, quickly drawing miners and prospectors. The 2020 census counted 20,961 people.
